reason: The cited evidence supports the synthesis, spray-coating, and low friction/wear of 2D HEA nanoflakes at room temperature under high load, but it provides no data above room temperature, no evidence on CoCrFeNi substrates, and actually shows failure in water, undermining the claim of broad environmental robustness. The key premise of high-temperature tribofilm stability is entirely unsupported.
premises: 2D HEA nanoflakes can be synthesized and spray-coated onto a substrate
The coating exhibits low friction and wear under high load in ambient conditions
Stress-induced tribocatalytic activity of the nanoflakes facilitates self-lubrication
The tribological performance is highly dependent on the solvent/medium used during coating
The coating can form a stable, low-shear tribofilm effective from RT to 800 °C
